transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-29 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Raj (Nimbus Head of Platform), Sofia (Nimbus ML Eng), Dan (Nimbus CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, just to kick off, i'm maya chen, AE on the account. um quick round robin?
[00:08] Raj: raj here — head of platform at nimbus. we've got sofia on for model integration and dan for platform questions.
[00:15] Liam: liam o'connor, solutions engineer. i'll cover the integration patterns and benchmarks.
[00:20] Dan: dan kim, cto. we'll mostly listen, ask about security and operational controls.

[00:28] Maya: quick agenda — integration patterns (sdk, langchain, llamain — sorry, llama index), gateway/proxy and network, quotas/rate limits, and observability hooks, then next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Raj: yep, sounds good. our main drive is to get an internal assistant on product pages with low latency and then expand to a personalized recommendations assistant.

[01:05] Sofia: just to set expectations, our current infra is hybrid — most traffic in aws us-west, some on-prem for PCI workloads. we use a centralized api gateway and have teams building with langchain and llamaindex.

[01:30] Liam: ok, good context. on the sdk side, we have official python and node sdks, plus examples for langchain and llamaindex connectors. the integrations are basically wrappers around our http api; for langchain we provide a small adapter class that maps calls and streaming.
[01:49] Sofia: can you share that adapter? we've got some custom chains and want to avoid rewriting.

[02:02] Maya: yes - we'll share a repo link after the call. it's got examples for prompt templating and streaming.

[02:20] Raj: how opinionated is the sdk? like does it force you into certain prompt formats or can we pass raw prompts and control tokenization?
[02:30] Liam: you can pass raw prompts. we expose parameters for max_tokens, temperature, stop sequences. we also surface model variants and quantization profiles when appropriate. SDKs intentionally thin — they focus on auth, retries, and streaming; mapping layer for langchain/llamaindex handles prompts.

[03:05] Dan: about deployment — if we start with hosted, what are the hooks we need to run through our gateway? i.e. egress IPs, mutual tls, or do you have a proxy option?
[03:18] Liam: for hosted we have a public endpoint with fine-grained api keys and IP allowlists. some customers place a proxy in front for egress control; others use our private deployment option which sits inside a VPC. we also support mutual tls for dedicated/private but for hosted typically ip allowlist + SSO and short-lived tokens.

[03:50] Sofia: so if we keep an internal gateway, do you recommend routing all calls through it or call redwood directly from services?
[03:58] Liam: common pattern is internal gateway for audit and routing; gateway handles batching and prefix caching, then fan out to redwood. that gives you central rate limiting and observability. alternatively, you can call redwood directly from services and use the sdk to attach request metadata and traces.

[04:30] Raj: ok — on quotas, we have multiple product teams; need per-team quotas and alerting. can redwood do that?
[04:38] Maya: yes — we have rate limits and quota scoping at api-key and team level. quotas are configurable and we expose metrics per key in the console and via prometheus/otel endpoints for Dedicated/Private. Hosted exposes dashboards and per-route breakdowns.

[05:05] Sofia: prometheus/otel — is that push or pull? how do we wire into our existing observability?
[05:12] Liam: Dedicated/Private ships an OTLP endpoint that you can scrape or forward to your collector, and we can export metrics to prometheus. Hosted provides webhooks and a metrics export job or an agent for forwarding. there are some differences in retention and granularity between hosted and dedicated.

[05:45] Dan: security checklist: SOC2, data residency, KMS for encryption, RBAC, SSO. do you have docs?
[05:52] Maya: yes, we have a security pack. we'll send SOC2 attestation, encryption at rest/in transit details, and dedicated KMS integrations for Private. we also support SAML SSO and role-based access in the console.

[06:15] Raj: for PCI-relevant flows we'd probably need private or on-prem. is that correct?
[06:22] Liam: typically yes; customers with strict PCI or data residency requirements prefer Private (VPC-hosted) or on-prem. Dedicated can be acceptable if your DPO signs off and logs/audit controls meet requirements. we'll surface the details in the security docs.

[06:45] Sofia: one technical ask — adapter for llamaindex. we use llamaindex to build our vector store flows. how seamless is it?
[06:53] Liam: we've got an unofficial integration in the examples repo that shows chunking, embeddings calls, and reranking. for embeddings we support batching and a dedicated endpoint; also we have token-aware batching to reduce cost.

[07:18] Raj: embeddings pricing and quotas — do you separate that from generation tokens?
[07:25] Maya: yes, embeddings are metered separately. quotas can be set per product team and you can assign different rate limits for embeddings vs generation endpoints.

[07:50] Dan: about latency — we need p95 under 180ms for small prompts in the us-west region. can you meet that on hosted?
[07:58] Liam: depends on model and sequence length; for smaller open models on hosted in us-west we've seen p95 around 120-150ms for short prompts with streaming disabled. if you need tighter/lower variance, Dedicated with reserved GPUs in-region is the recommended path. also network hops via a proxy add latency.

[08:35] Sofia: any auto-batching that increases latency? we rely on sync calls for low-latency.
[08:42] Liam: our runtime uses adaptive batching; for low-latency SLOs we can configure a threshold to minimize batching delay; Dedicated also gives more predictable batching because you can reserve capacity.

[09:05] Raj: can we pin model versions? we want deterministic outputs for tests.
[09:10] Maya: yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts and canary deploys — there's a console setting and api flags.

[09:28] Dan: observability hooks again — trace ID propagation and cost per token breakdowns?
[09:33] Liam: yes — sdk supports trace_id propagation in headers; you get per-request cost and token breakdowns in the console. for Dedicated/Private we expose token-level telemetry via otel and prometheus and you can add custom labels for routing.

[09:58] Sofia: about a gateway/proxy pattern — if we put a proxy in our VPC that pins to dedicated endpoints, do you support static backend ips?
[10:07] Liam: Dedicated can have static egress ips and VPC peering options; Private on-prem gives full control. Hosted only supports ip allowlist per api key — those are public endpoints.

[10:30] Maya: do you have any existing constraint on traffic shape? like bursty traffic or predictable spikes?
[10:36] Raj: we'll have spikes during product launches; baseline maybe 500 rps across teams and spikes up to 3k rps during campaigns.

[10:50] Liam: for that shape, Dedicated with autoscaling and burst capacity is a good fit; hosted could work for POC but might throttle if you exceed quota and you don't have reserved capacity. we can show cost/latency delta in the benchmark.

[11:15] Sofia: what about local caching or KV cache for session-based assistants?
[11:22] Liam: we support prefix and kv caching at the routing layer; SDKs can also maintain local caches. caching reduces token usage and latency for repeated prefixes. we'll include examples.

[11:45] Dan: compliance — audit logs for every prompt and response? we need an audit trail but redaction is important for pii.
[11:53] Maya: audit logs available in Dedicated/Private with configurable retention. we also have redaction helpers and can disable transcript storage for sensitive flows. for hosted we have configurable retention windows and export options.

[12:20] Raj: ok this is great. i want to talk about a small POC: run our sample prompt set across hosted and dedicated to compare p95 and cost. is that doable?
[12:30] Liam: yes — we'll need sample payloads, expected concurrency, and which models to test. we'll run benchmark script and share results.

[12:45] Sofia: can that use our existing langchain flows? we don't want to rework them.
[12:50] Liam: yes — the langchain adapter lets you run the same chains, just swap the llm wrapper to use redwood endpoints. we'll include a notebook.

[13:10] Dan: about rate limits — is there a way to failover to a smaller model under high load automatically?
[13:17] Liam: yes — smart routing policies can failover to cheaper/compatible model variants when capacity constrained. we can set rules by percent or latency thresholds.

[13:38] Raj: what about function calling / structured outputs? our assistant needs to call internal APIs.
[13:45] Maya: supported. we have function calling and structured output schemas; SDKs help marshal responses. we'll share examples for that too.

[14:05] Sofia: any pitfalls reading from S3 for context? we have doc loaders in llamaindex that pull s3 objects.
[14:12] Liam: those are common — performance depends on your pre-processing. we recommend pre-chunking and caching vectors; during the POC we can test the end-to-end flow including s3 fetch latency.

[14:35] Dan: ok what's next, concretely?
[14:40] Maya: next steps recap — share sdk/langchain/llamaindex examples, security pack, benchmark template. schedule a poc scoping meeting to nail the sample set and timeline.

[15:00] Raj: sounds good. one operational Q — pricing model: are embeddings and generations billed differently and can we get committed capacity pricing?
[15:10] Maya: embeddings and generation billed separately. we have usage-based hosted pricing and committed reserved pricing for Dedicated. we'll include preliminary pricing scenarios in the follow-up.

[15:30] Sofia: do you have case studies for retail ecommerce use cases?
[15:36] Maya: yes — we'll drop two short case studies and a benchmark heatmap that shows latency/cost tradeoffs.

[15:50] Dan: any red flags so far on our end?
[15:54] Liam: nothing immediate. the three areas to validate in the POC: latency p95, audit/redaction behavior, and VPC/egress requirements for PCI flows.

[16:12] Raj: timeline — we want a POC in January, about 2 weeks of benchmarking and then decision by end of January.

[16:25] Maya: ok we'll aim to have materials by next week and schedule the scoping call — i'll send a calendar invite.

[16:40] Sofia: small note — we use an internal billing center per team, will need per-team cost breakdowns.

[16:47] Liam: we output per-key cost metrics and can map api keys to teams, that should cover it.

[17:05] Dan: great. thanks all.

[17:10] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up — link to repo and security pack coming.

[17:20] Raj: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript. (Transcription includes occasional mishears, names may be slightly off e.g., "llamain" for LlamaIndex in a few spots.)
